narms_pct_resistant_{category}.short_description: Percentage of isolates showing resistance to {category.short_name}.
narms_pct_resistant_{category}.long_description: Percentage of isolates tested by NARMS showing resistance to {category.short_name}, based on CLSI breakpoints. Calculated as narms_n_resistant_{category} divided by narms_n_tested_{category}, multiplied by 100. In the resistance pattern file the category is a multi-drug resistance pattern rather than a single agent, and the value is the percentage of isolates matching that pattern. Cells with no measurement are NA rather than a sentinel value, because 0 is a legitimate result for this measure and could not be distinguished from a placeholder. The matching narms_flag_{category} column records why a cell is empty. A 0 here is a real finding only where the flag reads tested or tested_no_mic: it means isolates were tested and none were resistant.
narms_pct_resistant_{category}.statement: In {location}, {value}% of isolates were resistant to {category.short_name}

narms_n_tested_{category}.long_name: Number of isolates tested for susceptibility to {category.short_name}
narms_n_tested_{category}.short_description: Total isolates tested for resistance to {category.short_name}.
narms_n_tested_{category}.long_description: Total number of isolates tested for susceptibility to {category.short_name}. Denominator of narms_pct_resistant_{category}. Cells with no measurement are NA rather than a sentinel value, because 0 is a legitimate result for this measure and could not be distinguished from a placeholder. The matching narms_flag_{category} column records why a cell is empty. A 0 here is ambiguous on its own: it covers both no_isolates_tested, where the agent was on the panel but no isolates were available, and not_tested, where the agent was not on the panel for that row. Only the flag separates them.

narms_mic50_{category}.short_description: Median MIC across isolates tested for {category.short_name}.
narms_mic50_{category}.long_description: The concentration in micrograms per millilitre at which 50% of isolates are inhibited, i.e. the median MIC, calculated from isolate-level data. Present only in the FDA retail meats, animal pathogen, and food-producing animal files; the human clinical files report aggregate resistance percentages only. Missing values are NA: a concentration of 0 does not occur on the MIC scale, so filling it would invent a measurement. In the food-producing animals file, streptomycin carries a susceptibility interpretation but no concentration in roughly 99% of its rows, because three of the four FDA source spreadsheets publish an STR SIR column with no matching STR concentration column. Those rows are flagged tested_no_mic.

narms_mic90_{category}.long_description: The concentration in micrograms per millilitre at which 90% of isolates are inhibited, i.e. the 90th percentile MIC, calculated from isolate-level data. Present only in the FDA files. Missing values are NA for the same reason as narms_mic50_{category}, and the same streptomycin limitation applies.

narms_flag_{category}.long_name: Why a measurement for {category.short_name} is present or absent
narms_flag_{category}.short_description: Categorical flag explaining whether the values for {category.short_name} are real.
narms_flag_{category}.long_description: Records whether the value columns for {category.short_name} hold a real measurement, and if not, why not. Values are mutually exclusive; every cell carries exactly one, and a single row will normally contain several different values across its columns. tested: isolates were collected, the agent was on the panel, and results came back; the counts and percentage are real, and a 0 percent means none were resistant. no_isolates_tested: the agent was on the panel and tracked for that organism, geography and year, but no isolates were available to test. CDC reports this as an explicit zero, meaning we looked and there was nothing, as distinct from we did not look. Occurs only in the human clinical files, since the FDA files aggregate isolate records and a group with no isolates produces no row. not_tested: the agent was not part of the panel run for that specific combination of organism, geography, year and test method, although it is used against that organism elsewhere in the file. Causes include agents added to or dropped from panels partway through the surveillance period, narrower panels in some states, and recent years where collection and testing are still in progress. In the human files this is overwhelmingly state-level and concentrated in the most recent years, which are preliminary and will partly resolve to tested in future releases. not_on_panel: the agent is never used against that organism, in any geography, year or test method. Not a gap but a combination that does not exist as a clinical question, and it will never fill in. Arises because each file holds the union of every organism's panel in one set of columns. tested_no_mic: isolates were tested and the counts and percentage are real, but no MIC was published. Occurs only in the food-producing animals file. Rows flagged this way contain valid resistance measurements, so filtering on a flag equal to tested alone will silently exclude them; match both tested and tested_no_mic to select all real resistance measurements.

genus_species_serotype.long_description: Bacterial genus, species and serotype combined into a single label, with any absent part omitted. Present in the human clinical, retail meats and food-producing animal files. The human files use CDC's curated 30 species and serotype entries, including rollups such as All nontyphoidal; the FDA files report raw serotypes, giving 221 combinations in retail meats and 638 in food animals, of which 628 are Salmonella.

genus.short_description: Bacterial genus the resistance measurements describe.
genus.long_description: Bacterial genus. Used in the animal pathogen file, which reports at genus level only and covers E. coli, Klebsiella spp, S. pseudintermedius and Salmonella.

test_method.short_description: Whether results come from phenotypic or genotypic testing.
test_method.long_description: AST is phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing, available from 1999. WGS is whole genome sequencing, available from 2016 onward; there are no WGS rows before that year. The two methods give different results for the same organism and agent and are kept as separate rows rather than combined. Present in the human clinical files only.

meat_source.short_description: Retail meat product the isolate was recovered from.
meat_source.long_description: Retail meat product sampled, such as chicken, ground beef, ground turkey, pork chops or veal. Present in the retail meats file only.

host_species.short_description: Animal the isolate was recovered from.
host_species.long_description: Animal host the isolate was recovered from. In the food-producing animals file this covers cattle, chickens, swine, turkeys and minor species such as goats, lambs and sheep, along with eggs and ready to eat products. In the animal pathogen file the isolates are from dogs.

source_type.short_description: Sampling programme the isolate was collected under.
source_type.long_description: Sampling programme and stage, such as HACCP slaughter surveillance or cecal sampling broken out by animal type. Present in the food-producing animals file only.

collection_source.short_description: Clinical site the diagnostic isolate came from.
collection_source.long_description: Clinical site the isolate was collected from, such as urinary tract infections or other tissues and body sites. Because testing is driven by what a veterinarian ordered for a given case rather than a fixed panel, the set of agents tested varies by collection source within the same year. Present in the animal pathogen file only.

narms_now.name: NARMS Now: Human Data - Antimicrobial Resistance
narms_now.location: NARMS Now Interactive Dashboard - Human Data
narms_now.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
narms_now.description: Detailed antimicrobial resistance data from NARMS human clinical isolates, including resistance by individual antimicrobial agent (with CLSI class) and by resistance pattern (multidrug resistance profiles). Data available for 30 species/serotypes across 5 genera (Campylobacter, E. coli O157, Non-cholera Vibrio, Salmonella, Shigella), tested against 22 antimicrobial agents and summarised into 29 resistance patterns. Both AST (phenotypic) and WGS (genotypic) test method results are available; WGS coverage begins in 2016. Data span 1999-2025. Records from years after 2021 are preliminary, since isolate collection and testing are still in progress, and a substantially higher share of those cells is flagged 'not_tested' as a result. Data extracted from the NARMS Now Power BI dashboard. Suggested citation: CDC. National Antimicrobial Resistance Monitoring System (NARMS) Now: Human Data. Atlanta, Georgia: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.
narms_now.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

narms_retail_meats.name: FDA NARMS Retail Meats Surveillance Data
narms_retail_meats.organization: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Center for Veterinary Medicine
narms_retail_meats.description: Isolate-level antimicrobial susceptibility data from the FDA NARMS retail meats program. Samples collected from retail stores in participating states. Organisms tested include Campylobacter (coli, jejuni), Enterococcus (faecalis, faecium), Escherichia coli, and Salmonella (multiple serotypes), giving 221 distinct genus/species/serotype combinations tested against 31 antimicrobials. Meat sources include retail chicken, ground beef, ground turkey, pork chops, and veal. SIR (Susceptible/Intermediate/Resistant) calls based on CLSI breakpoints. Data span 2002-2021. Because this file is built by aggregating isolate-level records, a group with no isolates produces no row rather than a zero, so the 'no_isolates_tested' flag value does not occur here.
narms_retail_meats.restrictions: Public domain. FDA data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

narms_animal_pathogen.name: FDA NARMS Animal Pathogen Surveillance Data
narms_animal_pathogen.organization: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Center for Veterinary Medicine
narms_animal_pathogen.description: Antimicrobial susceptibility data from the FDA NARMS animal diagnostic pathogen surveillance program. Isolates submitted by veterinary diagnostic laboratories across the United States, covering 4 genera (E. coli, Klebsiella spp, S. pseudintermedius, Salmonella) tested against 74 antimicrobials. SIR calls based on CLSI breakpoints. Data available at state level and span 2017-2024. Because testing is driven by what a veterinarian ordered for a specific clinical case rather than by a fixed sampling panel, roughly half of the 'not_tested' cells in this file fall in years where the same organism and antimicrobial pairing was tested in a different host species or collection source. The 'no_isolates_tested' flag value does not occur here, since the file is built by aggregating isolate-level records.
narms_animal_pathogen.restrictions: Public domain. FDA data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

narms_food_animals.name: FDA NARMS Food-Producing Animals Surveillance Data
narms_food_animals.organization: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Center for Veterinary Medicine
narms_food_animals.description: Isolate-level antimicrobial susceptibility data from four FDA NARMS food-producing animal surveillance programs: (1) HACCP slaughter surveillance (1997-present), covering federally inspected slaughter and processing plants; (2) Cecal sampling at slaughter (2013-present), testing cecal contents from food animals; (3) Minor Species (2020-2022), covering less common food animal species. Organisms include Campylobacter, E. coli, Enterococcus, and Salmonella, giving 638 distinct genus/species/serotype combinations, of which 628 are Salmonella serotypes, tested against 35 antimicrobials. SIR calls based on CLSI breakpoints. National-level data only (no state breakdown). Data span 1997-2023. This is the only file in which the 'tested_no_mic' flag value occurs, almost entirely for streptomycin: three of the four source spreadsheets publish an 'STR SIR' interpretation column without a corresponding 'STR' concentration column, so resistance counts are available while MIC values are not. Because the file is built by aggregating isolate-level records, the 'no_isolates_tested' flag value does not occur here.
narms_food_animals.restrictions: Public domain. FDA data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.
